key_insight: The paper introduces IncrementalExecution, an online shot-allocation framework that stops sampling when additional shots stop meaningfully changing a circuit’s empirical output distribution.
engineering_relevance: It helps reduce quantum hardware time and cost by giving practitioners a practical way to choose near-minimal shot counts for static circuits on current cloud backends.
method: Black-box shot optimization with no assumptions about circuit structure or noise model
Incremental execution monitors distribution changes after each batch of shots
Supports customizable stopping and shot-management policies
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated across 33,750 framework configurations on 180 static circuit-backend pairs, totaling 7.3 million independent experiments.
watch_item: Because it is designed for static circuits in a black-box setting, performance and stopping behavior may vary when applied to highly nonstationary noise or adaptive workflows.
paper_title: How Many Shots Are Enough for a Quantum Circuit?
